title_en: 277: Global Equity Markets: Can the Stock Market Rally Continue Beyond AI?
title_zh: 全球股市：AI 之外的涨势能否延续？——对话 BlackRock 的 Carrie King 与 Alex Brazier
subtitle_zh: BlackRock 投资主管解读 AI 资本开支回报、市场集中度，以及 AI 之外全球股市的投资机会。
summary_zh: 本期 The Bid 由 Oscar Pulido 请来 BlackRock 全球基本面股票业务首席投资官 Carrie King 与全球投资及组合解决方案主管 Alex Brazier，讨论当下的核心问题：在 AI 之外，全球股市的涨势能否延续。Brazier 勾勒情绪：全球市场年初至今涨约 30%、8 月起横盘，投资者平均温和看多（mildly bullish），却出现罕见分歧——同一批受访者对加仓与减仓都回答是。他把这种分裂归因于 AI 建设（AI buildout）本身：相关股票涨了约 40%，而美股里只有约三分之一的股票在其 50 日均线（50-day moving average）上方交易，半导体单日涨跌超 5% 的天数比过去 24 年任何一个夏天都多——即便相信长期回报，也必须承认这是长久期（long duration）、波动极大的押注，仓位取决于目标与波动承受力。King 从盈利侧给出证据：自 2022 年 11 月 ChatGPT 发布以来 S&P 500 市值几乎翻倍，回报大部分由盈利驱动而非估值重估；一致预期未来五年 AI 建设累计投入还会约 7 万亿美元，判断能否兑现的关键在于回报何时到来——最近一季财报已看到当下的回报。她还指出两条 AI 之外的独立线索：一是过去一年报告从 AI 中获得经济收益的医疗健康公司数量增长 50%，构成很好的分散化选择；二是美国底层经济的周期性复苏——PMI 显示制造业与服务业已连续六个月扩张、盈利从负转正——与 AI 顺风彼此独立。Brazier 补充，新兴市场（emerging markets）敞口上全球投资者约净 20% 想加仓，但资金流沿着 AI 与非 AI 的分界线分布。谈到 AI 之外的配置，Brazier 坦言缺乏把握（conviction），倾向用市场中性策略（market-neutral strategy）赚取内部相对变动；King 则坚守医疗健康这条黑马之选。是一堂把 AI 交易拆成盈利、波动、集中度与分散化的实务课。

turns.en: Over the past three years, US stocks have delivered a remarkable run of strong returns, supported by corporate earnings, enthusiasm around artificial intelligence, and significant investment in new technologies. But with a handful of companies driving much of the market's performance, investors are
turns.zh: 过去三年，美股交出了一段相当亮眼的强劲回报，背后支撑的是企业盈利、市场对人工智能（AI）的热情，以及对新技术的大笔投入。但由于只有一小撮公司在拉动大盘的大部分表现，投资者正

turns.en: increasingly asking whether this momentum can continue and what opportunities might exist beyond the biggest names in US technology. You say to people, do you plan to add to your exposure or reduce your exposure? And the only consistent answer is yes.
turns.zh: 越来越想知道，这股势头还能不能延续，以及在美国科技巨头之外还有哪些机会。你问大家，是打算加仓还是减仓？唯一一致的回答是：都要。

turns.en: I think the question about sustainability becomes, what is your conviction that this massive spending on this AI buildout will continue? So what's really driving stock markets today? Are corporate earnings keeping pace with investor expectations? And as AI reshapes the investment landscape, where else around the world might investors
turns.zh: 我觉得，关于可持续性的问题就变成了：你有多大把握，认为这场 AI 建设（AI buildout）上的巨额投入还会继续？那么，如今真正在驱动股市的到底是什么？企业盈利有没有跟上投资者的预期？而随着 AI 重塑投资格局，全球其他地方还有哪些地方能让投资者

turns.en: find opportunities for growth and diversification? Welcome to the bid, where we break down what's happening in the markets and explore the forces changing the economy and finance. I'm Oscar Polito. Today, I'm joined by Carrie King, BlackRock's global chief investment officer of fundamental
turns.zh: 找到增长和分散化的机会？欢迎来到 The Bid，在这里我们拆解市场正在发生的事，探讨那些改变经济和金融的力量。我是 Oscar Pulido。今天和我一起的嘉宾是 Carrie King，她是 BlackRock 全球基本面

turns.en: equities, and Alex Brazier, global head of investment and portfolio solutions at BlackRock. Together, we'll explore what's behind the recent strength in equity markets, how investors are thinking about AI and market concentration, and where opportunities may be emerging across global equities as we look toward year end.
turns.zh: 股票业务的首席投资官，以及 Alex Brazier，他是 BlackRock 全球投资与组合解决方案主管。我们一起探讨近期股市强势背后的原因、投资者如何看待 AI 和市场集中度，以及在临近年底之际，全球股市中哪些地方可能正在浮现机会。

turns.en: Alex and Carrie, thank you so much for joining us on the bid. Really great to be back with you, Oscar. Thank you, Oscar. It's nice to be here. And it's great to have you both on. I've spoken to both of you individually, but we've never had you together on the same episode.
turns.zh: Alex、Carrie，非常感谢你们两位做客 The Bid。真的很高兴又能和你一起，Oscar。谢谢你，Oscar，很高兴来到这里。能有你们两位一起来真是太好了。我之前分别和你们俩都聊过，但还从没把你们请进同一期节目。

turns.en: And I'm excited about the expertise that sits between the two of you in terms of markets, and we're going to talk equities a little bit more specifically. Alex, you and I last spoke before the summer, and we were talking to yourself into Sam Vekt about emerging markets. There's been a lot happening in equity markets since then.
turns.zh: 我很期待你们两位在市场方面带来的专业洞见，今天我们会更具体地聊聊股票。Alex，你和我上次聊还是在夏天之前，当时我和你还有 Sam Vekt 一起谈的是新兴市场（emerging markets）。从那以后，股市发生了不少事。

turns.en: So what are some of the key themes that you're hearing from investors over the last few months? It feels like about 100 years ago that we last spoke about these things. What are we hearing? The background context is that the market globally is up about 30% year to date, pretty respectable, but it's chopped sideways since early August.
turns.zh: 那么，过去几个月你从投资者那里听到的一些关键主题是什么？感觉我们上次聊这些话题都像是 100 年前的事了。我们都听到了些什么？大背景是，全球市场年初至今涨了大约 30%，相当可观，但自 8 月初以来一直在横盘震荡。

turns.en: We've been surveying lots of investors since then to ask about their sentiment and their plans. And their sentiment, I would say, on average, is mildly bullish. And that's true in every part of the world, Asia, Europe, US as well. So even though the market's gone sideways, there's still a little bit bullish,
turns.zh: 从那以后，我们调查了很多投资者，问他们的情绪和打算。我会说，他们的情绪平均来看是温和看多（mildly bullish）的。而且全球每个地区都是如此，亚洲、欧洲、美国也一样。所以尽管市场在横盘，大家还是有点偏乐观，

turns.en: still a bit of optimism out there. And that's very different from where we were in the second quarter, when people were pretty bearish. But I think the really interesting thing to me is that average masks really big differences of view. You say to people, do you plan to add to your exposure or reduce your exposure?
turns.zh: 市场上还是有一些乐观情绪。这和我们二季度时的状态很不一样，那时候大家相当看空（bearish）。但我觉得真正有意思的是，这个平均值掩盖了观点上非常大的分歧。你问大家，是打算加仓还是减仓？

turns.en: And the only consistent answer is yes. They are especially so about US equities, where we have lots of people responding to the question, do you plan to add? Yes. And lots of people responding to the question, do you plan to reduce your exposure to express yes? Just take here in Europe, when we survey people, we've got about
turns.zh: 唯一一致的回答是：都要。美股尤其如此，很多人对'你打算加仓吗'这个问题回答'是'，同时也有很多人对'你打算减仓吗'这个问题也回答'是'。就拿欧洲来说，我们调查时，大约有

turns.en: a third of respondents saying, I want to add, and a third saying, I want to subtract my exposure to US equities. And that is a really unusual level of difference of view. I think behind that is a question about the AI buildout, which has been a real driver of the market. We think stocks associated with the AI buildout are up by about 40%.
turns.zh: 三分之一的受访者说'我想加仓美股'，另外三分之一说'我想减仓美股'。这种观点分歧程度非常罕见。我认为背后是一个关于 AI 建设的问题，而 AI 建设一直是市场真正的驱动力。我们估计，与 AI 建设相关的股票上涨了大约 40%。

turns.en: And they're up over recent months. That's what the market's been reliant on. Only about a third of stocks in the US market are trading above their 50-day moving average. So investors are asking about future returns around the AI buildout, which the market's relied.
turns.zh: 而且它们是在最近几个月里涨上来的。这正是市场一直依赖的东西。美股市场里只有大约三分之一的股票在其 50 日均线（50-day moving average）上方交易。所以投资者在问，围绕着市场所依赖的 AI 建设，未来的回报会怎样。

turns.en: But I think the other interesting thing there is they're asking about volatility, which isn't that common. They are asking, the summer has been a volatile one. If that continues, how much of this trade do I actually want? Because we saw loads of headlines over the summer. And when you look at semiconductors, the heart of the AI trade,
turns.zh: 但我觉得另一个有意思的地方是，他们在问波动性（volatility）的问题，这并不常见。他们在问，今年夏天一直波动很大，如果这种情况持续下去，这笔交易我到底想要多少仓位？因为整个夏天我们看到了大量新闻头条。而当你看半导体——这个 AI 交易的核心——

turns.en: they were up or down more than 5% or more days than any summer for the last 24 years. The AI trade, even if you're a great believer in the long run returns associated with it, you know it's going to come with a lot of volatility. And that's because it's a long duration play.
turns.zh: 它们单日涨跌超过 5% 的天数，比过去 24 年里任何一个夏天都多。AI 这笔交易，即便你非常相信它长期能带来的回报，你也知道它会伴随着很大的波动。原因在于它是一个长久期（long duration）的押注。

turns.en: So small differences of view day to day can make a big difference to your view. And that's why I think people are taking different approaches because even if you have the same view about the long run here, the right investment choice for you actually depends on
turns.zh: 所以，每天观点上的细微差别，可能会让你的整体判断产生很大的不同。这也是为什么我觉得大家在采取不同的做法：因为即便你对长期前景的看法一致，对你而言正确的投资选择其实取决于

turns.en: what are you trying to achieve? Are you a shorter term investor who really cares about volatility? Those people are stepping back. Or are you a really long term investor who can just ride it all out and wait for those long run returns? And I think it's really useful reminder actually that the
turns.zh: 你到底想实现什么目标？你是一个真的很在意波动性的短线投资者吗？这类人正在退场。还是说你是一个真正的长期投资者，可以扛过这一切、等待那些长期回报？我觉得这其实是一个非常有用的提醒：那笔

turns.en: right investment depends on much on what are you trying to achieve as it does on what do you think about the world? And I think that last point is important because when you said the view is bullish or mildly bullish, that could reflect the longer term view that people seem to share. But then
turns.zh: 正确的投资，在多大程度上取决于'你想实现什么'，就在多大程度上取决于'你如何看待这个世界'。我觉得最后这点很重要，因为你说情绪是看多或温和看多，那可能反映的是大家似乎都认同的更长期看法。但随后，

turns.en: the specific action that people want to take in portfolios, whether to add or reduce, might come down to the specific investment outcome that they're trying to generate. You also mentioned equities have had a good year. Kerry, US stocks have been at the center of
turns.zh: 大家在组合中想采取的具体行动，无论是加仓还是减仓，可能取决于他们想要实现的具体投资结果。你还提到股票今年表现不错。Carrie，美股一直处在

turns.en: that strong year, another year of double digit returns so far for the US stock market. Can you talk us through what have been some of the key drivers of those returns? And what's your outlook for the continuation of the strong returns in the US market? So it's been more than a couple of
turns.zh: 这个强劲年份的核心，到目前为止美国股市又是双位数回报的一年。你能给我们讲讲，这些回报的一些关键驱动因素是什么吗？对于美股强势回报能否延续，你又怎么看？——所以这已经不只是

turns.en: years. Let's go back all the way to when chat GPT emerged on the scene. A new artificial intelligence tool is going viral for cranking out entire essays in a matter of seconds. Two weeks ago, a new artificial intelligence program called chat GPT made its debut online this project. It was November
turns.zh: 两三年的事了。我们一路回到 ChatGPT 刚登场的时候。'一款新的人工智能工具，因为能在几秒钟内生成整篇文章而迅速走红。两周前，一个名叫 ChatGPT 的新人工智能程序在网上首次亮相。'那是在

turns.en: 2022. Since that launch of chat GPT, the S&P 500 is just about doubled in value.
turns.zh: 2022 年 11 月。自从 ChatGPT 那次发布以来，S&P 500 的市值几乎翻了一倍。

turns.en: Most of that stark market return is driven by actual earnings growth rather than any kind of revaluation of the companies. So when you disaggregate that doubling of market value during that period, since that launch of chat GPT that S&P 500 earnings were up 75% in that period,
turns.zh: 这段惊人的市场回报，大部分是由实打实的盈利增长驱动的，而不是对公司的任何重新估值。所以当你把这段时间——自 ChatGPT 发布以来——市值翻倍的来源拆开来看，S&P 500 的盈利在此期间上涨了 75%，

turns.en: higher company valuations did contribute, but to a lesser extent, the price earnings multiple, which is a measure of that, went from just under 18 times earnings to about 19 times today. So about an 8% revaluation. And then dividends cumulatively over that period added about
turns.zh: 更高的公司估值确实有贡献，但程度较小。衡量这一点的市盈率（price earnings multiple）从略低于 18 倍盈利涨到了今天的大约 19 倍。所以大约 8% 的重新估值。然后，在此期间股息累计又贡献了大约

turns.en: another 10%. So stock market returns very much driven by actual earnings growth, not just sentiment.
turns.zh: 另外 10%。所以股市回报在很大程度上是由实实在在的盈利增长驱动的，而不仅仅是靠情绪。

turns.en: And then when we look under the hood of the index level earnings growth, what we see is that it was dominated as you won't be surprised by tech. But you can also see the progression of the AI trade from sort of the picks and shovels, semis, the hardware, the memory, into the broader
turns.zh: 然后，当我们深入去看指数层面的盈利增长时，会发现——你也不会意外——它是由科技股主导的。但你也能看到 AI 交易的演进：从那种'卖铲子'的环节，也就是半导体、硬件、存储，扩展到更广泛的

turns.en: infrastructure buildout, which includes data centers, power, select industrials like electoral equipment, cooling equipment. You ask about the future and the sustainability Oscar. I think the question about sustainability becomes, what is your conviction that this massive spending on this
turns.zh: 基础设施建设，包括数据中心、电力，以及一些特定的工业板块，比如电气设备、冷却设备。Oscar，你问到了未来和可持续性的问题。我觉得关于可持续性的问题就变成了：你有多大把握，认为这场

turns.en: AI buildout will continue? So let's just investigate that for a minute. The consensus view right now is that there will be about another $7 trillion of cumulative spending on the AI buildout over the next five years. So how does one garner any confidence that's actually going to happen?
turns.zh: AI 建设上的巨额投入还会继续？那我们就来研究一下这个问题。目前的一致预期是，未来五年 AI 建设上的累计投入还会再有大约 7 万亿美元。那么，一个人要怎么才能对'这真的会发生'建立起一些信心呢？

turns.en: The key determinant to answer that question is when and will these companies earn any kind of a return on that massive spending? In the recent second quarter earnings period, we're absolutely seeing a return being generated today. So the hyperscalers, the companies that are spending all of this money
turns.zh: 回答这个问题的关键决定因素是：这些公司什么时候、以及能否从这笔巨额投入中赚到任何回报？在最近的二季度财报季，我们确确实实看到了当下正在产生的回报。所以那些超大规模云厂商（hyperscalers），也就是砸下这一切资金的公司，

turns.en: saw a meaningful acceleration and the revenue of their cloud business. And what this measures and can confirm is that their spending is absolutely enabling increased AI usage. So let me just walk you through the numbers because they're pretty astonishing. The cloud revenue again, a measure of
turns.zh: 它们云业务的营收出现了明显的加速。这衡量并且能够证实的是，它们的投入确实在推动 AI 使用量的增长。那我来带你过一遍这些数字，因为它们相当惊人。再看一下云营收，也就是衡量

turns.en: AI usage from the top three hyperscalers accelerated from 15% growth in the second quarter last year to nearly 50% in the second quarter this year. And even more acceleration is on tap for Q3. And let me just highlight how impressive that growth rate is when you consider this fact.
turns.zh: AI 使用量的指标：前三大超大规模云厂商的云营收增速，从去年二季度的 15% 加快到了今年二季度的近 50%。而且三季度还会有更多加速。我再强调一下，当你考虑到这个事实时，这个增长率有多惊人。

turns.en: There was 50% growth on the revenues, but those revenues themselves were double. So an accelerating growth rate on a higher earnings base. So really powerful growth that we're seeing, which I think underpins the argument that we'll see continued upside in the long term opportunity
turns.zh: 营收增长了 50%，但营收基数本身已经翻倍了。所以是在一个更高的盈利基数上还在加速的增长率。这是我们看到的非常强劲的增长，我认为它支撑了这样一个论点：我们会看到长期机会上持续的上行空间

turns.en: for AI. And one of the things that you mentioned, Kerry, was that the bulk of the returns in the US stock market over the last couple of years have come from earnings growth and not necessarily higher valuations. Kerry also mentioned, though, the AI build out the trillions of dollars in
turns.zh: ——指的是 AI 的长期机会。你提到的一点，Carrie，是说过去几年美股的大部分回报都来自盈利增长，而不一定是更高的估值。不过 Carrie 还提到了 AI 建设，提到了数以万亿美元计的

turns.en: CapEx. This has been a big question hanging over the market. When will the return on investment come? It sounds like it is coming. But Alex, what are you hearing about the AI exposure that people have in their portfolios? How are they feeling about it? And what do they want to do or what can they do
turns.zh: 资本开支（CapEx）。这一直是悬在市场头顶的一个大问题：投资回报什么时候到来？听起来它正在到来。但是 Alex，关于大家组合里的 AI 敞口，你都听到了些什么？他们对此感觉如何？他们想做什么，或者他们能做什么

turns.en: if they want to diversify outside of AI? I'd say this is like the number one topic in terms of portfolio conversations. Because as you say and built on what Kerry was saying, the earnings growth that we've seen has been pretty concentrated. And that's now reflected in a concentration of market
turns.zh: ——如果他们想在 AI 之外做分散化的话？我会说，这几乎是组合讨论里的头号话题。因为正如你所说，也在 Carrie 观点的基础上延伸，我们所看到的盈利增长是相当集中的。而这如今反映在市场

turns.en: capitalization, which to emphasize what you both said, isn't to do with valuations and hope about the future. It's actually reflecting what's happening on the ground now, as Kerry was saying. So it's not an issue per say, but it is making people think, okay, I have a lot of exposure to this
turns.zh: 市值的集中度上。为了强调你们两位说的，这并不是关乎估值和对未来的期望。它其实反映的是当下正在实际发生的事，就像 Carrie 说的那样。所以这本身并不是一个问题，但它确实在让大家思考：好，我在这个

turns.en: AI build out theme. How do I manage that? And I think the first thing is they want to measure it. And measuring it involves taking a different look at the portfolio to a normal split.
turns.zh: AI 建设主题上有很大敞口。我该怎么管理它？我觉得首先，大家想要衡量它。而衡量它，就需要用一种不同于常规划分的方式来看组合。

turns.en: A normal split might be, I've got US equities, I've got UK equities, I've got European equities, I've got EM equities. This, you want to abandon all the borders and look at each stock and ask, is this an AI build out trade stock? And I'm going to put a different lens on the portfolio
turns.zh: 常规的划分可能是：我有美股、英股、欧洲股票、新兴市场（EM）股票。而这里，你要抛弃所有的地域边界，逐只看每一只股票，问：这是不是一只 AI 建设交易的股票？我要用一副不同的镜头来看组合，

turns.en: and look at it based on its exposure to the AI build out wherever it is. And its exposure to not the AI build out. And then people make their decision, as I said before, based on their appetite for volatility, partly, as to what that split's going to be.
turns.zh: 根据它对 AI 建设的敞口来看它，不管它在哪里；还有它对'非 AI 建设'的敞口。然后，正如我之前说的，大家会基于自己对波动性的承受意愿，部分地来决定这个划分会是什么样。

turns.zh: 那些并没有真正集中在 AI 建设上的部分，自夏初以来已经跌了大约 5%。所以问题与其说是'多少 AI、多少非 AI'，不如说是：我到底该怎么构建组合里那个'非 AI'的部分，才不至于只是买入一大堆将要
